summary: Revision 2026-07-28 has no negotiation handshake: every request carries `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]` (required) and `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"]` (required), optionally `clientInfo` and `logLevel`; on HTTP the version is mirrored in the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header, which MUST match the body. A server that does not implement the requested version MUST answer with `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` (code -32022, `data.supported: string[]`, `data.requested: string`; HTTP 400). Clients SHOULD pick a mutually supported version from `supported` and retry, else surface an error. Servers MUST implement `server/discover` (params: only `_meta`; result: `resultType`, `supportedVersions`, `capabilities`, optional `instructions`, `ttlMs`, `cacheScope`, `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"]` SHOULD). Calling it is optional for clients; it is the stdio era-probe. Extensions are negotiated via the `extensions` map in ClientCapabilities/ServerCapabilities keyed by `_meta`-style identifiers with mandatory prefix; if only one side supports an extension the supporter MUST fall back to core behaviour or reject with an error. Dual-era rules: a recognized modern JSON-RPC error (-32020/-32021/-32022, or 404+-32601 on HTTP) identifies a modern server, anything else (or timeout on stdio, or 4xx without modern body on HTTP) identifies a legacy server and triggers fallback to `initialize`; fallback MUST NOT be keyed to one error code; era is cached per server process/origin. A dual-era server selects era from how the client opens (`_meta` present vs `initialize`), MAY serve both concurrently, and a modern-only server SHOULD name its supported versions in the error it returns to `initialize`. Error-code policy: -32020..-32099 are spec-reserved; -32002 and -32042 MUST NOT be emitted. Every result MUST carry `resultType`; absent means `"complete"` from legacy servers.

methods.name: server/discover
methods.capability_gate: None. Servers MUST implement it unconditionally (discover.md 'Discovery' intro; versioning.md 'Protocol Version Negotiation'; schema.ts DiscoverRequest doc). Clients MAY call it (not required).
methods.params: `params: RequestParams` = `{ _meta: RequestMetaObject }` and nothing else ('The request carries no body parameters beyond the standard _meta', discover.md 'Request'). RequestMetaObject (schema.ts L63-111): `"io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": string` (REQUIRED), `"io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": ClientCapabilities` (REQUIRED; `{}` = no optional capabilities), `"io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo"?: Implementation` (optional, SHOULD be sent), `"io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel"?: LoggingLevel` (optional, deprecated SEP-2577), `progressToken?: string|number` (optional), plus any other `_meta` keys following the naming rules (`traceparent`/`tracestate`/`baggage` allowed without prefix). JSON-RPC envelope: `jsonrpc:"2.0"`, `id: string|number`, `method:"server/discover"`. Example id in spec: "discover-1".
methods.result: `DiscoverResult extends CacheableResult extends Result` (schema.ts L678-697, L1081-1110, L223-236): `resultType: "complete" | "input_required" | string` (REQUIRED on servers of this version; for `server/discover` in practice `"complete"`); `supportedVersions: string[]` (REQUIRED; 'The client should choose a version from this list for use in subsequent requests'); `capabilities: ServerCapabilities` (REQUIRED); `instructions?: string` (optional; natural-language guidance for LLMs, should not duplicate tool descriptions); `ttlMs: number` (REQUIRED via CacheableResult, integer >= 0 ms, HTTP max-age semantics; caching.md L15-18 lists server/discover among operations that MUST carry caching hints); `cacheScope: "public" | "private"` (REQUIRED via CacheableResult); `_meta?: ResultMetaObject` where `"io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"?: Implementation` SHOULD be included (discover.md 'DiscoverResult'; basic/index.md 'Per-response protocol fields'); `[key: string]: unknown` index signature (extra fields allowed). Wrapped as `DiscoverResultResponse { jsonrpc, id, result: DiscoverResult }`. Not paginated. NOTE: there is NO top-level `serverInfo` or `protocolVersion` field in DiscoverResult (unlike legacy InitializeResult); identity lives only in `_meta`.
methods.notes: Errors: if the requested version is unsupported -> UnsupportedProtocolVersionError -32022 (HTTP 400); if required `_meta` fields missing -> -32602 Invalid params (HTTP 400); HTTP header/body mismatch -> -32020 HeaderMismatch (HTTP 400). On HTTP, request also needs `MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method: server/discover` headers (streamable-http.md 'Standard Request Headers'; `Mcp-Name` not required for this method). Serves two documented purposes: presenting server info (capabilities/identity/versions in one request instead of tools/list+prompts/list+resources/list) and stdio backward-compat probe (discover.md 'When to Call'). `serverInfo` is self-reported: clients SHOULD NOT change behaviour on it nor rely on it for security.

methods.name: (implicit) any request — per-request version declaration
methods.capability_gate: None; applies to every request in the modern era.
methods.params: Every request's `params._meta` MUST carry `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` (string) and `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities` (ClientCapabilities); SHOULD carry `io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo` (Implementation) (basic/index.md 'Per-request protocol fields'; versioning.md 'Protocol Version Negotiation').
methods.result: Any Result MUST carry `resultType` (schema.ts Result L229) and SHOULD carry `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"]`. On unsupported version the response is `UnsupportedProtocolVersionError` (below) instead of a result.
methods.notes: The server accepts or rejects each request independently; no state from prior requests may be used (basic/index.md 'Statelessness': servers MUST NOT rely on prior requests for capabilities/version/identity; schema.ts L96 'Servers MUST NOT infer capabilities from prior requests').

methods.name: UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (error response shape, not a method)
methods.capability_gate: None; returned by any modern server for any request whose declared version it does not implement.
methods.result: JSON-RPC error response: `{ jsonrpc:"2.0", id: RequestId (optional in JSONRPCErrorResponse type, but echoes request id in examples), error: { code: -32022, message: string (example 'Unsupported protocol version'), data: { supported: string[] (REQUIRED, versions the server supports), requested: string (REQUIRED, the version the client asked for) } } }` (schema.ts L483-501; versioning.md example L56-69). HTTP status MUST be 400 Bad Request (schema.ts L475-476; streamable-http.md 'Protocol Version Header').
methods.notes: Returned whether the version is unknown or a known version the server chose not to support (versioning.md L50-54; schema.ts L473-475). A recognized modern error: on receipt a dual-era client MUST NOT fall back to `initialize` (stdio.md L138-141).

methods.name: HeaderMismatchError (error response shape)
methods.result: `{ error: { code: -32020, message: string } }`; `data` not defined for this error in the schema (schema.ts L463-470). HTTP status MUST be 400 (streamable-http.md 'Server Validation').
methods.notes: Returned when `MCP-Protocol-Version` header != `_meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` (schema.ts L71-72; streamable-http.md L257-261), or when a required standard header (`MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method`, `Mcp-Name`) is missing/malformed. Counts as a recognized modern error for era detection (streamable-http.md 'Backward Compatibility' L651-657).

methods.name: MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (error response shape)
methods.capability_gate: Emitted when a request needs a client capability not declared in `_meta.io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities`.
methods.result: `{ error: { code: -32021, message: string, data: { requiredCapabilities: ClientCapabilities } } }` (schema.ts L513-526; basic/index.md L389-394). HTTP status MUST be 400.
methods.notes: Counts as a recognized modern error for era detection (streamable-http.md L651-657). Distinct from -32601 which is used for server-side capability gating (schema.ts L346-348).

methods.name: initialize (LEGACY, 2025-11-25 and earlier; only relevant for dual-era support)
methods.capability_gate: None in legacy; not part of 2026-07-28. A modern-only server treats it as an unknown method.
methods.params: Legacy (2025-11-25_schema.ts L255-272): `params: { protocolVersion: string, capabilities: ClientCapabilities, clientInfo: Implementation, _meta? }`.
methods.result: Legacy `InitializeResult`: `{ protocolVersion: string, capabilities: ServerCapabilities, serverInfo: Implementation, instructions?: string, _meta? }`; no `resultType`. Followed by client notification `notifications/initialized` (no response).
methods.notes: On a modern-only server: stdio -> a JSON-RPC error with implementation-defined code (unknown method + missing required `_meta`); the server SHOULD name its supported protocol versions in that error (versioning.md L156-159, matrix row Legacy/Modern). HTTP -> 400 per server validation (missing required headers). A dual-era server answers `initialize` and serves that client under the negotiated legacy revision, scoped to the stdio process or the HTTP session (versioning.md L176-182).

requirements.text: If the server does not implement the requested protocol version (unknown, or known but not supported), it MUST respond with an UnsupportedProtocolVersionError (code -32022) listing the versions it does support in `data.supported` and echoing `data.requested`.
requirements.cite: versioning.md 'Protocol Version Negotiation' L50-69; schema.ts UnsupportedProtocolVersionError L472-501

requirements.text: On HTTP, the UnsupportedProtocolVersionError response status MUST be 400 Bad Request.
requirements.cite: schema.ts L475-476; streamable-http.md 'Protocol Version Header' L263-267

requirements.text: On UnsupportedProtocolVersionError the client SHOULD select a mutually supported version from `data.supported` and retry the request, or surface an error to the user if no compatible version exists.
Servers MUST implement `server/discover`.
requirements.cite: versioning.md L75-76; discover.md L9-11; schema.ts DiscoverRequest doc L655-658; changelog.md Major change 3

requirements.text: Clients MAY call `server/discover` before sending other requests to learn supported versions up front; they are not required to and may invoke any RPC inline and handle UnsupportedProtocolVersionError.
requirements.cite: versioning.md L76-80; discover.md 'When to Call' L66-69

requirements.text: Every request MUST include `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]` (string) and `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities"]` (ClientCapabilities).
requirements.cite: basic/index.md 'Per-request protocol fields' L369-379; schema.ts RequestMetaObject L69-98; versioning.md L45-46

requirements.text: A request missing any required `_meta` field is malformed; the server MUST reject it with JSON-RPC -32602 (Invalid params); on HTTP the status MUST be 400 Bad Request.
Clients SHOULD include `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo"]` (Implementation with required `name` and `version`) on every request unless specifically configured not to.
requirements.cite: basic/index.md L386-387; schema.ts L78-80; discover.md request example

requirements.text: Servers SHOULD include `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo"]` (Implementation) in every result, including DiscoverResult, unless configured not to.
requirements.cite: discover.md 'DiscoverResult' L100-101; basic/index.md L398-404; schema.ts ResultMetaObject L145-147

requirements.text: clientInfo and serverInfo are self-reported and unverified; implementations SHOULD NOT use them to change behaviour and SHOULD NOT rely on them for security decisions.
requirements.cite: discover.md Note L105-110; basic/index.md L406-412; schema.ts L85-88, L152-155

requirements.text: Servers MUST include `resultType` on every result; DiscoverResult additionally MUST carry `supportedVersions`, `capabilities`, `ttlMs` (>= 0) and `cacheScope` ("public"|"private").
requirements.cite: schema.ts Result L229, DiscoverResult L678-697, CacheableResult L1081-1110; caching.md L15-18, L62

requirements.text: When a result from a server implementing an earlier protocol version omits `resultType`, the client MUST treat it as "complete".
requirements.cite: schema.ts Result L230-232; changelog.md Major change 8

requirements.text: Servers MUST NOT rely on prior requests over the same connection/process to establish context (capabilities, protocol version, client identity); MUST NOT infer capabilities from prior requests.

A server MUST NOT rely on capabilities the client has not declared; if a request needs an undeclared client capability it MUST return MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (-32021) with `data.requiredCapabilities`; HTTP status MUST be 400.

Extension identifiers used as keys in `capabilities.extensions` MUST follow the `_meta` key naming rules and MUST have a prefix (prefix is mandatory for extension ids, optional for general _meta keys).
requirements.cite: versioning.md 'Extension Negotiation' L84-89; schema.ts L779-780, L876-877

requirements.text: If one party supports an extension but the other does not, the supporting party MUST either revert to core protocol behaviour or reject the request with an appropriate error.
Extensions SHOULD document their expected fallback behaviour.

`_meta` key format: optional prefix = dot-separated labels + '/', labels start with a letter and end with letter/digit (interior letters/digits/hyphens); name (unless empty) MUST start and end with [a-z0-9A-Z], interior may include '-', '_', '.'; any prefix whose second label is `modelcontextprotocol` or `mcp` is reserved for MCP. Implementations SHOULD use reverse-DNS prefixes. Implementations MUST NOT make assumptions about values at reserved keys.
A server MAY implement both legacy (`initialize` handshake) and modern (per-request `_meta`) behaviours (dual-era).

A dual-era server MAY serve both eras concurrently on the same endpoint or process; it selects era per how the client opens: modern `_meta` request -> stateless modern handling; `initialize` -> legacy semantics scoped to the stdio process or HTTP session.
A modern-only server SHOULD name the protocol versions it supports in any error it returns to an `initialize` request, on any transport (legacy clients have no fall-forward).

stdio: a dual-era client SHOULD probe with `server/discover` before any other request, with its preferred modern version in `_meta`. Outcomes: DiscoverResult -> modern (pick from `supportedVersions`); recognized modern error (e.g. -32022) -> modern, use `supported`, do NOT fall back; any other error or no response within a reasonable timeout -> legacy, fall back to `initialize`.
requirements.cite: stdio.md 'Backward Compatibility' L130-144; versioning.md L138-140; discover.md L78-83

requirements.text: The stdio fallback MUST NOT be keyed to one specific error code; legacy servers answer unknown pre-initialize requests with implementation-defined errors (commonly -32601 or -32602) or not at all.

A modern-only client on stdio does not need to probe but probing is RECOMMENDED because some legacy servers process era-ambiguous methods (e.g. tools/call) under legacy semantics; probe yields deterministic failure. Matrix Modern/Legacy: on stdio clients SHOULD send server/discover first.
requirements.cite: stdio.md L150-154; versioning.md matrix row 'Modern | Legacy' L169

requirements.text: HTTP: a dual-era client MAY detect era by attempting a modern request first; on 400 Bad Request it SHOULD inspect the body: recognized modern JSON-RPC error -> modern, retry with advertised versions or correct the request; empty body or unrecognized error -> fall back to `initialize` and continue legacy.

Era determination is a property of the server; clients SHOULD cache it for the lifetime of the server process (stdio) or origin (HTTP), and MAY persist it across restarts of the same server configuration, re-probing if the cached assumption later fails.
HTTP: every POST to the MCP endpoint MUST include the `MCP-Protocol-Version` header and its value MUST match `_meta["io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion"]`.
HTTP: on header/body mismatch or missing/malformed required header the server MUST reject with 400 Bad Request and a JSON-RPC error with code -32020 (HeaderMismatch).
HTTP: if the server does not implement the requested RPC method it MUST respond 404 Not Found with JSON-RPC error -32601 (distinguishes it from a legacy HTTP+SSE 404).

HTTP: a server supporting clients earlier than 2025-06-18 MAY treat a request without `MCP-Protocol-Version` as version 2025-03-26; a server not supporting such clients MUST reject requests lacking the header per server validation.
HTTP modern-only server receiving legacy traffic SHOULD: respond 405 Method Not Allowed to GET/DELETE on the MCP endpoint; ignore `Mcp-Session-Id` (never mint/echo); ignore `Last-Event-ID`.

Implementations MUST NOT emit codes from -32020..-32099 not defined by the spec and MUST use defined codes only with their specified meanings; MUST NOT allocate new codes in -32000..-32019 (SHOULD NOT use that range at all); MUST NOT emit -32002 or -32042 (clients SHOULD still accept -32002 from older servers). New application codes SHOULD be outside -32768..-32000.

Clients MUST NOT serve a cached DiscoverResult (or other cacheable result) for a request whose method or parameters differ; results carrying `inputResponses`/`requestState` MUST NOT be cached; caches with cacheScope "private" MUST NOT be shared across authorization contexts.
requirements.cite: caching.md L29-39, L103; schema.ts CacheableResult L1103-1106

requirements.text: ttlMs: 0 -> immediately stale (MAY re-fetch each time); positive -> consider fresh that many ms; absent -> assume 0; negative -> ignore, treat as 0.
Clients and servers MAY support multiple protocol versions simultaneously.

Clients that render icons (Implementation.icons) MUST support image/png and image/jpeg (and image/jpg); SHOULD support image/svg+xml and image/webp; consumers SHOULD verify icon URLs are same-domain/trusted and take precautions with SVG.

wire_details: Protocol version constant: LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = "2026-07-28"; JSONRPC_VERSION = "2.0" (schema.ts L30-32). Legacy constants: 2025-11-25_schema.ts LATEST_PROTOCOL_VERSION = "2025-11-25"; 2025-06-18_schema.ts = "2025-06-18". Other versions named in the material: "2025-03-26" (header-less fallback value), "2024-11-05" (HTTP+SSE).

_meta keys (exact): "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion" (string, required on requests); "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities" (ClientCapabilities, required on requests); "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientInfo" (Implementation, optional/SHOULD); "io.modelcontextprotocol/logLevel" (LoggingLevel, optional, deprecated); "io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo" (Implementation, optional/SHOULD on results); "io.modelcontextprotocol/subscriptionId" (RequestId, on subscription-stream notifications); "progressToken" (string|number); "traceparent", "tracestate", "baggage" (W3C formats, unprefixed exception).

Extension identifier examples (exact): "io.modelcontextprotocol/ui" (MCP Apps; settings example {"mimeTypes": ["text/html;profile=mcp-app"]}), "io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks" (settings {}), "io.modelcontextprotocol/oauth-client-credentials" (schema.ts L776). Keys of `capabilities.extensions` must have a mandatory prefix.

Error codes (exact): -32700 PARSE_ERROR; -32600 INVALID_REQUEST; -32601 METHOD_NOT_FOUND; -32602 INVALID_PARAMS (also used for missing required _meta fields, resource-not-found replacement); -32603 INTERNAL_ERROR; -32020 HEADER_MISMATCH; -32021 MISSING_REQUIRED_CLIENT_CAPABILITY; -32022 UNSUPPORTED_PROTOCOL_VERSION. Reserved never-reuse: -32002 (legacy resource not found), -32042 (2025-11-25 URL elicitation required). Draft-era renumbering (changelog Minor 12): HeaderMismatch -32001 -> -32020, MissingRequiredClientCapability -32003 -> -32021, UnsupportedProtocolVersion -32004 -> -32022. Ranges: -32000..-32019 implementation-defined/legacy; -32020..-32099 spec-reserved.

MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError data: {"requiredCapabilities": ClientCapabilities}. HeaderMismatchError: no data field defined; example message 'Header mismatch: Mcp-Name header value 'foo' does not match body value 'bar''.

HTTP headers: `MCP-Protocol-Version: 2026-07-28` (required on every POST; must equal body _meta value); `Mcp-Method: <method>` (required all requests); `Mcp-Name` (required for tools/call, resources/read, prompts/get from params.name or params.uri); `Mcp-Param-{Name}` (custom, Base64 sentinel encoding permitted); legacy headers to ignore on modern-only server: `Mcp-Session-Id`, `Last-Event-ID`.

HTTP status codes: 400 Bad Request for -32020, -32021, -32022 and for missing required _meta (-32602); 404 Not Found + -32601 for unknown method; 405 Method Not Allowed for GET/DELETE on a modern-only MCP endpoint; legacy HTTP+SSE detection: 400/404/405 without recognized modern JSON-RPC body -> GET expecting SSE `endpoint` event.
ResultType enum: "complete" | "input_required" | string (open). cacheScope enum: "public" | "private". ttlMs: integer milliseconds >= 0 (example 3600000).
Icon.theme enum: "light" | "dark"; Icon.sizes strings "WxH" (e.g. "48x48") or "any"; icon MIME types: image/png, image/jpeg, image/jpg (MUST), image/svg+xml, image/webp (SHOULD).

ClientCapabilities (schema.ts L716-786) exact fields, all optional: experimental?: {[k]: JSONObject}; roots?: {} (deprecated; NO listChanged sub-field in 2026-07-28); sampling?: { context?: JSONObject, tools?: JSONObject } (deprecated); elicitation?: { form?: JSONObject, url?: JSONObject }; extensions?: {[extensionId]: JSONObject}. No `tasks` field (moved to extension).

ServerCapabilities (schema.ts L793-883) exact fields, all optional: experimental?: {[k]: JSONObject}; logging?: JSONObject (deprecated); completions?: JSONObject; prompts?: { listChanged?: boolean }; resources?: { subscribe?: boolean, listChanged?: boolean }; tools?: { listChanged?: boolean }; extensions?: {[extensionId]: JSONObject}. No `tasks` field.

Implementation (schema.ts L976-997) = BaseMetadata + Icons + own: name: string (REQUIRED); version: string (REQUIRED); title?: string; description?: string; websiteUrl?: string (uri); icons?: Icon[] where Icon = { src: string (uri, REQUIRED), mimeType?: string, sizes?: string[], theme?: "light"|"dark" }.

JSONObject = { [key: string]: JSONValue } with JSONValue = string|number|boolean|null|JSONObject|JSONArray (schema.ts L6-12). RequestId = string | number. JSONRPCErrorResponse.id is optional in the type.

Conformance: check id `server-stateless:sep-2575-server-implements-discover` (conformance_README.md L234); `--requirements 2026-07-28` runs the stateless wire, `2025-11-25` runs the initialize wire; a scenario in both sets must pass under both (L137-150). Tier 1 via `tier-check --requirements 2025-11-25,2026-07-28`.

Inspector era model (docs inspector protocol-eras.md): protocolEra = legacy | auto | modern; auto = probe server/discover then fall back to initialize on any non-modern outcome; legacy is the default because probing stalls against silent legacy stdio servers (timeout matters).
sdk_implications: Server core: register a built-in, always-on `server/discover` handler returning {resultType:'complete', supportedVersions, capabilities, instructions?, ttlMs, cacheScope, _meta.serverInfo}. Make `supportedVersions`, `ttlMs` (default 0 or configurable) and `cacheScope` (default 'public' unless server data is per-user) configurable; never omit them.

Server core: per-request middleware that (1) validates presence/type of `_meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion']` and `_meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities']` -> -32602 (+HTTP 400) if missing; (2) checks the version against the configured supported list -> -32022 with data.supported/data.requested (+HTTP 400); (3) exposes the per-request ClientCapabilities/clientInfo/logLevel to handlers via a request-context object and never caches them across requests (statelessness).

Server core: helper to emit MissingRequiredClientCapabilityError (-32021, data.requiredCapabilities) from handlers that need e.g. elicitation; helper to gate unadvertised server methods with -32601 (HTTP 404).
Server core: attach `resultType` to every result (default 'complete') and `_meta['io.modelcontextprotocol/serverInfo']` unless disabled by config; provide a switch to suppress serverInfo.

Server HTTP transport: require and validate `MCP-Protocol-Version`, `Mcp-Method`, `Mcp-Name` (numeric comparisons numerically, Base64 sentinel decoding for Mcp-Name/Mcp-Param-*) -> 400 + -32020; unknown method -> 404 + -32601; GET/DELETE -> 405; ignore Mcp-Session-Id/Last-Event-ID; optional config to treat header-less requests as 2025-03-26 when legacy support is enabled.

Server dual-era option: if `initialize` is received, switch that stdio process / HTTP session to legacy 2025-11-25 semantics (InitializeResult with protocolVersion/capabilities/serverInfo/instructions, notifications/initialized, Mcp-Session-Id etc.); if disabled, answer `initialize` with an error whose message names the supported modern versions. Modern `_meta` requests must remain servable concurrently in the same process.

Client core: PowerShell client object holds `PreferredProtocolVersion`, `SupportedProtocolVersions`, `ClientInfo` (name/version required; title/description/websiteUrl/icons optional), `ClientCapabilities` (experimental/roots/sampling/elicitation/extensions) and `SendClientInfo` flag; every outgoing request is stamped with the three `_meta` keys; optional per-request logLevel/progressToken/trace keys; `_meta` key validation against the naming regex (labels, prefix, reserved second-label check).

Client core: automatic retry-on--32022: parse `error.data.supported`, intersect with own supported set (preserving own preference order), re-send once with the chosen version, remember it per server; raise a typed exception if the intersection is empty. Treat -32020/-32021/-32022 (and HTTP 404+-32601) as 'recognized modern errors'.

Client core: `Invoke-McpDiscover` / `Get-McpServerInfo` cmdlet returning a typed DiscoverResult (SupportedVersions, Capabilities incl. Extensions map, Instructions, ServerInfo from _meta, TtlMs, CacheScope) with an optional local cache keyed by method+params honoring ttlMs/cacheScope semantics (0/absent/negative => stale).

Client core: era detection state machine per server (stdio process / HTTP origin): Modern | Legacy | Unknown, with configurable probe timeout on stdio, fallback not keyed to any specific error code, optional persistence across restarts and automatic re-probe on failure; expose protocolEra setting = legacy|auto|modern like the Inspector. On HTTP: on 4xx inspect body for recognized modern error before falling back; then optionally fall back further to HTTP+SSE (GET, expect `endpoint` event).

Client core: when Legacy, run the 2025-11-25/2025-06-18 `initialize` + `notifications/initialized` flow, map legacy InitializeResult (top-level serverInfo/protocolVersion) into the same typed server-info object, and default absent `resultType` to 'complete'; support legacy `roots.listChanged`, `tasks` capability fields only in legacy mode.

Types: model ClientCapabilities/ServerCapabilities as open objects (index signature) with `extensions` as a hashtable of extensionId -> settings object; validate extension ids (mandatory prefix). Provide an extension registry so that a party supporting an extension the peer lacks can either fall back to core behaviour or reject with an error (per-extension policy hook).

Error taxonomy: strongly typed PowerShell exceptions/records for HeaderMismatch (-32020), MissingRequiredClientCapability (-32021), UnsupportedProtocolVersion (-32022, with Supported/Requested), plus standard JSON-RPC codes; never emit -32002/-32042 or undefined codes in -32020..-32099; accept -32002 from legacy servers; keep local errors (timeouts) distinguishable from peer errors.

Conformance: plan to pass `server-stateless` (incl. check `sep-2575-server-implements-discover`) under `--requirements 2026-07-28` and the initialize-based scenarios under `--requirements 2025-11-25` if dual-era is claimed; CI baseline file may list `<scenario>:<check-id>` entries.
legacy_delta: Handshake removed: 2025-11-25/2025-06-18 required `initialize` (params protocolVersion, capabilities, clientInfo) + `notifications/initialized`; 2026-07-28 has no handshake, version/capabilities/identity travel per request in `_meta` (changelog Major 2; versioning.md 'Terminology'). Legacy InitializeResult had top-level `protocolVersion`, `capabilities`, `serverInfo`, `instructions`; modern DiscoverResult has `supportedVersions` (array, not a single negotiated version), `capabilities`, `instructions`, and serverInfo only inside `_meta`.
Legacy rule 'if the client cannot support the server-chosen protocolVersion it MUST disconnect' (2025-11-25_schema.ts L281) is replaced by per-request UnsupportedProtocolVersionError + client retry.

`server/discover` is new (does not exist in 2025-11-25 or earlier); on legacy servers it yields implementation-defined errors (commonly -32601/-32602) or silence, which is exactly the stdio detection signal.

Error codes: -32022/-32021/-32020 are new (draft numbers -32004/-32003/-32001 renumbered); -32002 resource-not-found (legacy) replaced by -32602; -32042 (2025-11-25 URL elicitation) removed. Clients SHOULD still accept -32002 from legacy servers.
`resultType` is new and required on all modern results; legacy results lack it and clients MUST default to 'complete'. `ttlMs`/`cacheScope` (CacheableResult) are new.

ClientCapabilities delta: 2025-06-18 had roots{listChanged?}, sampling: object, elicitation: object; 2025-11-25 added sampling{context?,tools?}, elicitation{form?,url?}, tasks{list?,cancel?,requests{sampling.createMessage?, elicitation.create?}}; 2026-07-28 removes `tasks` (now extension io.modelcontextprotocol/tasks), removes `roots.listChanged` (roots becomes `{}` and is deprecated), deprecates `sampling`, adds `extensions` map. `experimental` value type object -> JSONObject.

ServerCapabilities delta: 2025-11-25 had tasks{list?,cancel?,requests{tools.call?}}; 2026-07-28 removes `tasks`, deprecates `logging`, adds `extensions` map; prompts/resources/tools/completions/experimental unchanged in shape.

Implementation delta: 2025-06-18 = {name, version, title?}; 2025-11-25 added description?, websiteUrl?, icons?; 2026-07-28 identical to 2025-11-25 (name/version required; title/description/websiteUrl/icons optional).

HTTP transport delta relevant to versioning: `MCP-Protocol-Version` header existed since 2025-06-18 (absent before -> 2025-03-26 assumption MAY apply); 2026-07-28 additionally requires body/header match, `Mcp-Method`, `Mcp-Name`; removes Mcp-Session-Id, GET SSE stream, DELETE, Last-Event-ID and server-initiated requests. HTTP+SSE (2024-11-05) is Deprecated; clients MAY fall back to it after failing modern and legacy Streamable HTTP detection.

Removed methods affecting dual-era clients: `ping`, `logging/setLevel`, `notifications/roots/list_changed`, `resources/subscribe`/`unsubscribe`, `tasks/*` core methods, `notifications/elicitation/complete`; server-initiated requests replaced by MRTR (`resultType: 'input_required'`). A dual-era SDK must keep these only on the legacy code path.
Conformance runs the same scenarios under two wires: through 2025-11-25 stateful initialize; 2026-07-28 stateless per-request _meta; passing one says nothing about the other.
open_questions: `message` text of UnsupportedProtocolVersionError is illustrative ('Unsupported protocol version'); the spec does not mandate the exact string. Decide on a canonical message in the SDK.
No normative 'reasonable timeout' value for the stdio probe is given; the Inspector notes that probing stalls against silent legacy stdio servers. SDK must pick a default (and make it configurable).

The spec does not define what a server should return for an `initialize` request on a modern-only stdio server beyond 'implementation-defined code' and SHOULD-name-versions; choose between -32601 and -32602 and include supported versions in `message` (and possibly `data`), as no data shape is specified.
`data.supported` ordering is unspecified; whether it reflects server preference is not stated. Client selection policy (client-preference vs server-list order) must be an SDK decision.

How `server/discover` on a dual-era server should populate `supportedVersions` (modern versions only, or also legacy 2025-11-25?) is not specified; versioning.md example lists both '2026-07-28' and '2025-11-25' in `supported`, which suggests legacy versions may be listed, but a modern client cannot use a legacy version via per-request `_meta`.
Per-extension settings schemas (e.g. `mimeTypes` for io.modelcontextprotocol/ui) are defined in extension docs, not in the pages read here; SDK needs the extension pages for validation.

The legacy lifecycle pages (2025-11-25 version negotiation rules, e.g. server responding with a different version than requested, initialize retry rules) are not in the local corpus; fetch https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2025-11-25/basic/lifecycle.md via curl if full legacy behaviour is to be implemented.

JSONRPCErrorResponse.id is optional in the schema; whether a server may omit `id` on an UnsupportedProtocolVersionError for a parsable request is not stated (examples always echo it). SDK should always echo the id.
Whether `cacheScope` for `server/discover` should default to 'public' is not mandated; example uses 'public'.
